name: The kill switch, watched killing and sparing
non_visual_rationale: A verdict inside stored JSON and an apply seam that yields day-zero output; the day-zero degrade it guarantees is precisely that nothing visible changes wrongly.
criteria_delivered: 1. Rolling-origin blocked CV shipped in src/learning/cross-validation.ts: CV_SCHEME is the literal { kind: 'rolling_origin_blocked', train_weeks: [1,8], test_weeks: [9,10] } (05-03's declarations rule will read it as source text). The held-out block is the freshest 14 calendar days across the whole system's residual history (system-level, per 06 s7 G7 and adr-correction-gates-and-clamps decision 3); the judge compares mean ABSOLUTE error, corrected vs raw, on that block alone, per gated key.

2. The monthly job stays metrics-only: buildMonthlyMetrics (src/learning/metrics.ts) now computes cv.verdict for real via judgeRollingOriginCorrections instead of the deferred 'not_evaluated' literal, and writes it INTO the metrics file. No write to learned/corrections/v1/ was added anywhere; both 05-02 acceptance tests' snapshot-diff oracle (assertWritesConfinedToMetrics) prove the store outside learned/metrics/v1/ is byte-identical after the run, on both a kill month and a winning month.

3. src/learning/load-correction.ts's loadStoredCorrections now consumes the latest monthly verdict at load time: while it is corrections-killed, every spot whose OWN loaded record carries an applied key maps to null -- the same day-zero cost as an absent or corrupt file. corrections-stay, not_evaluated, and an absent/unreadable/unknown-value metrics file all leave the per-correction gates as the sole authority; only an affirmative 'corrections-killed' ever kills (proven by both ATs plus the appended fast-check property in tests/unit/learning-load-correction.test.ts covering the full probe vocabulary).

4. A winning month leaves every correction applying and is recorded distinctly: the a-winning-month-leaves-the-corrections-standing.test.ts AT proves the file states 'corrections-stay', the outcome's verdict agrees, and the apply lane still loads the stored record (b and applied untouched). A kill month's outcome additionally carries a distinguishing event (learning.cv.corrections_killed) beyond metrics_written, proven by the a-losing-month AT's events assertion (D-2026-08-12-1 pin 3).

5. cv.verdict is exactly one of corrections-killed | corrections-stay | not_evaluated everywhere it is produced or consumed, and outcome.verdict / the file's cv.verdict / the apply lane's behaviour never disagree: evaluate.ts reads metrics.cv.verdict for both the file write and the outcome, one computation, never recomputed a second way.
criteria_deferred: Judging score_delta corrections under the same monthly CV is NOT built: 06 section 10's metric table defines MAE only for height, and no acceptance or design text names a score-side CV metric. judgeRollingOriginCorrections and its gatedCorrections builder in metrics.ts are scoped to height keys only, documented as a flagged scope note in cross-validation.ts. A future slice that wants score corrections judged needs its own test driving that behavior.

The apply-seam metrics probe reuses loadStoredCorrections' existing CorrectionSource.getCorrection capability rather than a dedicated store method, per design direction (both 05-02 ATs hand a store implementing ONLY getCorrection). This means, in the real production wiring, BuildStore's getCorrection already IS a generic bucket read (confirmed in src/pipeline/adapters/s3-store.ts: getCorrection calls this.get(key)), so the probe works end to end without any ports.ts change -- but ports.ts itself was intentionally left untouched (outside this step's owned_paths) and carries no NEW named capability for reading learned/metrics/v1/; a future slice widening BuildStore should route through this same getCorrection-style generic read rather than adding a parallel one.

Upstream doc language still says 'applied: false EVERYWHERE' (06 s7 G7's own row text, adr-correction-gates-and-clamps decision 3, R34): this lane implements the corrected mechanism (apply lane maps applied-bearing records to null) but does not edit those upstream docs -- already flagged as owed back-propagation in wave-decisions.md D-2026-08-12-1's own 'Upstream issues flagged' section, not repeated here as new work.
scope_note: One real conflict surfaced during GREEN, resolved in-bounds rather than by editing an out-of-scope file. The 05-02 ATs hand loadStoredCorrections a store object implementing ONLY getCorrection, so the metrics-file probe has no channel but that same method -- there is no separate reader to inject without touching src/pipeline/ports.ts (not in owned_paths). Reusing getCorrection unconditionally, though, made every build call it for two extra learned/metrics/v1/ keys, which broke a PRE-EXISTING, sealed acceptance test from an earlier slice (tests/acceptance/.../a-correction-file-can-never-move-a-number-past-the-gates.test.ts, 02-03), whose own MemoryBuildStore test double records every getCorrection key and asserts the exact set with deepEqual. That test's own fixture uses a gate-refused correction (n=6, below G1's floor of 10) -- applied:false on every key. Resolution: loadStoredCorrections now only spends the verdict probe when at least one record it loaded this call actually carries an applied key (height or score_delta); a record with none is already the day-zero cost on its own, so a kill can change nothing about what it would publish, and the probe is skipped rather than spent on a question whose answer moves no number. This restored 02-03 to green (0 probe calls when nothing loaded is applied) while leaving both 05-02 ATs (whose fixture IS applied:true) and the new unit property (seeded with an explicitly applied fixture, appliedRecord(), rather than the parser-law tests' un-applied wellFormedRecord()) green. Verified: full suite before this fix showed exactly one new failure beyond the 5 named pre-existing ones (02-03's exact-key-list assertion); after the fix, that failure is gone and no other test changed state.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: Majority rule is over JUDGED (evaluable) gated keys, not over every gated key that exists. A gated key with zero training-period samples or zero held-out samples this month is left out of both the numerator and the denominator -- it was not evaluated, not spared, not judged a loser by default. Zero judged keys (including the case of zero gated keys at all) yields not_evaluated, generalizing pin 2's stated 'zero applied height keys' case. An exact tie (losingKeys*2 == judgedKeys) spares: the amended criteria say 'majority', which this reads as a STRICT majority (>50%), so a tie leaves corrections-stay. Pinned and tested (tests/unit/learning-cv-laws.test.ts, the tie-spares property).

The rolling origin is computed from the LATEST day any sample in the system was observed on (across every key, gated or not), never from the wall clock and never per key -- one shared origin for the whole system, matching 06 s7's own 'deliberately system-level, not per-spot' framing and the mined recover/learning-build reference. heldOutBlockStart is exported (not private) specifically so it is its own testable driving port, per nw-tdd-methodology's 'pure domain functions are their own driving ports' rule.

MAE, not block-bias magnitude (D-2026-08-12-1 pin 1): rawBlockError = mean(|residual|), correctedBlockError = mean(|residual - b|), b read from the stored record's own gated key, never re-fit. This module never re-fits anything; judging the fit that already shipped is its whole job.

The CV judge is scoped to height corrections only (see criteria_deferred). gatedHeightCorrectionsOf and datedHeightResidualSamplesOf in metrics.ts are new, separate passes over the same observations/predictions rows maeOf already reads, kept deliberately unshared with maeOf's own key-building: the CV judge and the displayed MAE are two different questions asked of the same rows, and entangling them would make either one harder to change alone.

The verdict-consumption metrics-key format (learned/metrics/v1/dt=<YYYY-MM>/metrics.json) is RESTATED in load-correction.ts rather than imported from evaluate.ts. evaluate.ts owns the monthly job's own heavier import graph (inputs.ts, metrics.ts, cross-validation.ts); pulling all of it into the build's hourly hot path merely to share one template string was judged the wrong trade, mirroring evaluate.ts's own precedent of restating fit.ts's fit-window boundary rather than importing it.

The apply-seam probe is bounded to applied-bearing loaded records (see scope_note). This is a genuine behavioral decision, not just a test-satisfying trick: a record with zero applied keys already publishes day-zero on that key regardless of the monthly verdict, so skipping the probe for it is output-identical to running the probe and getting 'not killed' -- the same reasoning G5/G6's own read-time-only clamps rest on.

The previous-month fallback in correctionsAreKilled first normalises to day 1 of the current month before subtracting a month (new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, 1)) then setUTCMonth(month-1)), specifically to avoid a day-31-into-February overflow bug that a naive setUTCMonth(now.getUTCMonth()-1) on the original instant could produce.
acceptance: Both pre-authored, JIT-distilled 05-02 acceptance tests, describe.skip removed (the only touch made to either file besides making loadStoredCorrections' input type real -- no oracle was edited). (1) a-losing-month-switches-the-corrections-off-until-a-human-looks.test.ts: ten weeks of playa-venao mornings, forty training mornings whose forecast runs -0.22 m, then a held-out fortnight that flips to +0.22 m; asserts assertWritesConfinedToMetrics reports exactly the one dt=2026-08 metrics key, cv.verdict is corrections-killed both in the file and in outcome.verdict, learned/corrections/v1/ is byte-identical before/after, the apply lane (loadStoredCorrections given the same store and clock) maps playa-venao to null, and outcome.events contains an entry naming corrections-killed. (2) a-winning-month-leaves-the-corrections-standing.test.ts: the same ten weeks, but the held-out fortnight keeps agreeing (-0.22 m throughout); asserts cv.verdict is corrections-stay in both file and outcome, learned/corrections/v1/ is untouched, and the apply lane still loads the stored record with its original b and applied:true intact.
unit_law: Five fast-check properties, driven only through each module's own exported pure functions (no private helpers exercised directly). tests/unit/learning-cv-laws.test.ts: (1) heldOutBlockStart sits exactly 13 days before the latest sampled day and every sampled day classifies as training-or-held-out, never neither, for any nonempty generated day set; (2) judgeRollingOriginCorrections reports not_evaluated exactly when there is no gated correction, or it has no training sample, or no held-out sample (all 8 boolean combinations exercised via fc.boolean() x3); (3) an exact tie between winning and losing judged keys always spares (corrections-stay), for any even key count 2..12; (4) mean absolute error flips a single gated key between corrections-stay and corrections-killed as the held-out residual flips between matching the correction (+b, credited) and doubling past it (-b, blamed), for any b in [0.05,2] and any small bounded noise -- the property that would fail under the ruled-out |mean(residual)| comparison. tests/unit/learning-load-correction.test.ts appended one Modeling-strategy (Hebert ch.3) property: a small reference oracle predicts, from the current-month and previous-month probe outcomes alone (killed/stay/not_evaluated/absent/corrupt/unknown-value, all 36 pairs), whether loadStoredCorrections must null an applied-bearing spot's record; the real loader is asserted to agree with the oracle on every pair, covering all seven named candidate cases (previous-month-probe is the (absent, killed) pair) in one test.
test_budget: 5 distinct behaviours (fold-boundary law, not_evaluated condition, majority-tie-spares, MAE credit/blame sign-flip, verdict-consumption-at-the-apply-seam) x 2 = budget 10. Delivered 5: one property per behaviour, no parametrize-inflation, no consolidation needed (nw-test-optimization skill section 4 procedure run before commit).
red_evidence: Both target ATs' describe.skip removed with production changes (evaluate.ts, metrics.ts, load-correction.ts, build.ts, cross-validation.ts) reverted to HEAD via a saved patch + git checkout (never git stash), then re-run: 'npx vitest run <the two 05-02 AT files>' collected 2 test files, 2 tests, 2 failed -- both semantic AssertionError on cv.verdict ('not_evaluated' received, 'corrections-killed'/'corrections-stay' expected respectively), zero collection or import errors. Production changes then restored via git apply of the same patch plus cross-validation.ts recreated from a saved copy; both ATs re-run green (2 passed).
falsifiability_evidence: Two controlled mutations, each reverted and diff-confirmed clean. (1) src/learning/cross-validation.ts: `correctedBlockError > rawBlockError` (a loss) flipped to `<` (a win): learning-cv-laws.test.ts's MAE sign-flip property failed, AND both target ATs failed (the kill scenario stopped reporting corrections-killed, the spare scenario's expectations also broke) -- reverted; `diff` against the pre-mutation saved copy showed byte-identical restoration. (2) src/learning/load-correction.ts: `current === "corrections-killed"` widened to also treat `current === "corrections-stay"` as a kill: the appended loader property failed, AND the winning-month AT failed (a winning month started degrading to day zero) -- reverted; re-ran the three affected files green to confirm the clean revert (git diff not usable here since HEAD already differs from this step's own baseline; re-running the tests to green is the confirmation).
gates_run: npm run typecheck: exit 0, twice (once after GREEN, once after both falsifiability reverts). Full suite (npx vitest run, no filter): 107 files -- 100 passed, 4 failed, 3 skipped; 537 tests -- 527 passed, 5 failed, 5 skipped. The 5 failures are exactly the pre-existing family named in this step's own task context (tests/unit/staleness-stamp.test.ts, staleness-stamp-format.test.ts, staleness-flip.test.ts, report-island.test.ts x2 -- the civil-day build refusal); this diff touches none of those files. Also separately confirmed: the AT's `applyLaneInput` object type-checks against loadStoredCorrections' real parameter type without its `as unknown as` cast (compiled a throwaway file importing loadStoredCorrections and calling it with the AT's exact object shape, no cast, exit 0) -- the widening the amended criteria asked for is real, not just accepted by the cast.
